final_timing_note: [dopa] seconds per frame, final mode (2048 spp, threshold 0.01, 1920x1080) on GPU 7, which two other builders also use. Gate stills: f16 30.3 s (wide), f75 43.2 s (macro), f140 35.9 s (wide). Strip f61-72: 57.4 s for f61 (first frame of its process, including setup), then 43.2, 49.1, 54.5, 70.9*, 106.2*, 87.9*, 42.8, 44.0, 42.9, 42.8, 42.8 s. The three starred frames coincided with other builders' renders. When nothing else was on GPU 7 (checked with nvidia-smi), the macro ran at about 43 s/f; the wide shot runs about 30-36 s/f. The mean of the unspiked gate frames is 42.9 s/f. That is slightly above the 40 s/f target, and the whole shot works out to roughly 1.8-2.0 GPU-h against the 1.5 planned. Three large costs were found and removed on the way: 179 s/f before fixes; about 200 s/f for any frame where the subdivided glass heart was moving; about 2x for meshes whose decay keys never reach zero. Not yet measured at final quality: the f1-14 orb drop and the f151-180 push. If time must come down, the cheapest lever is 1536 spp for the macro (f61-120).

deviations: Render setting, a storyboard spec bug: clamp_indirect 20 -> 0. The orb's radiance is about 250 (25 W over a 5 cm sphere), so clamp 20 scaled every refractive caustic sample down about 14x and the caustics vanished. The calibration script _caustics_test.py also used 0. The gate shows no fireflies.

Key light 250 W -> 21 W, plus a 10 W omni POINT 'OrbGlow' at the same point and radius, parented to the orb (the storyboard's risk-4 remedy, which lifts the walls to dim mint). Spot is 120 deg, blend 0.35, aimed at (-0.25,-0.35,0). During the f1-14 fall both powers scale with (z/0.95)^1.3 so f1 isn't murky. 250 W read about 1.0 on the floor.
Fill 60 W 'sky' -> 8 W 'cream', aimed at (0,0.6,0.6). At 60 W the fill read as bright as the key.
World: candy_sky_nosun at 0.08 for diffuse and transmission rays but 0.45 for glossy rays (Light Path mix), so chrome mirrors a bright candy sky while ambient stays low. camera_bg is mint at 0.18.
Room size 3.4 -> 4.2 and height 2.4 -> 2.5. At 3.4 m the mirror-ball push swept the room's front-right slab edge and wall end (dark void) through frame.

Layout: casters spread in a V opening toward the lens so no caustic lands on another caster: heart stand (0,0.15), lemon (-0.48,-0.12), ring (0.50,-0.15). Bunny and plinth moved to (-0.88,0.62), gold cone to (-0.42,1.30). Swirl moved to (0.98,1.12) and yawed -15 deg, because the orb at phi = 35 deg overlapped it.
Caster sizes: lemon ball r 0.13 -> 0.17; ring 0.15/0.05 -> 0.17/0.065.

Heart: an inflated, lens-shaped candy heart (34 cm tall, 5 cm thick, CDT-filled filleted outline, subsurf 2) replaces the extruded and bevelled slab. The slab's top cusp bevelled into a 40 cm spike, and a flat slab throws only a dim tinted shadow; the lens focuses a bright pink caustic. Tilt back stays at 10 deg. The tip is seated 12 mm into the stand.

Glass tint: Principled base colour = colour^0.5 (lemon ^0.35), because Cycles applies the tint at both interfaces (lemon squared reads amber, pink squared reads dark red). Lemon absorption 2.0 -> 1.0.

Cam W: 40 -> 55 mm and target (0.05,0.35,0.60). f121-150 uses ease_out_cubic into the push; the push runs prog(f,150,180) with ease_in_cubic and ends at d = 0.7896 m (exact 1536 px silhouette at 55 mm). The camera is baked to f181 so the f180 shutter blurs symmetrically. Focus ends at ball_c + 0.06u instead of ball_c - 0.08u, keeping the silhouette sharp. f-stop 3.5 -> 8 as specified.

Cam M: the 85 mm floor-skimming camera (z 0.24) became a 75 mm high-angle macro (z 1.85, about 33 deg). At z 0.24 the caustic band was about 55 px tall and unreadable. It trucks left (x 0.10 -> -0.04) with the caustics as the orb arcs right; f/5.6 and the orb stays above frame.

Fourth-wall card: 7x3.5 m at y = -7.5 became 13x8 m, centred on the ball's view axis at 7.2 m and facing the ball. Emission 0.35 -> 0.9, emission sampling NONE (a reflection card, never a sampled light).

Heart rock ends at its 2nd zero crossing (f61, matching 'at rest by f62'), and its object motion blur is keyed off from f47 (on during the fall). Ring wobble ends at its 5th zero crossing (f86). Swirl has object motion blur off (0.5 deg/f spin) and casts no shadow, because its blurred spiral shadow read as a dark disc on the wall. These are all render-cost and cleanliness changes.
Swirl is now a chrome lollipop with a gold axle stick and hub behind the disc (the storyboard's 6 cm stick could not reach the spinning disc).
known_issues: Render cost is about 43 s/f steady state in the macro and 30-36 s/f in the wide, slightly over the 40 s/f gate target. Whole-shot estimate is about 1.8-2.0 GPU-h against 1.5 planned. f1-14 and f151-180 were not timed at final quality. GPU sharing caused three gate frames to spike to 71-106 s.
The crystal bunny's rainbow caustics on the plinth and floor are subtle. The rainbow reads strongly inside the bunny, but the f16 'sparkle on plinth and floor' beat is weak at viewing size.
The pink heart caustic reads as a heart-shaped shadow with a pink glow and a hot centre, upside-down from the lens (lobes nearest the camera). It is not a crisply outlined heart.

The ring caustic hugs the ring: a bright aqua crescent at its front edge plus an arc inside the hole, not a separate ring on the floor. Its gate-region stability number is confounded by the ring's own wobble.

The f180 end frame is heavily zoom-blurred at the silhouette (53 px soft edge) because the push is at full ease-in-cubic speed into the cut. S03's first frame needs a similar pull-out blur for the match to feel continuous.
The floor pool reads about 0.73-0.83 near the orb, above the 0.55-0.70 target. It was left there to avoid a gloomy room; the caustics still read clearly.
f12-14: the orb's last fast frames before it stops produce a large lighting change (|delta| up to 14/255). It is intended as the drop-in, but it is a hard snap.
In the macro the lemon ball is partly cropped at the left edge, and the bunny and plinth peek in at the top-left corner.
The right pistachio wall reads slightly grey-green, and the left mint wall reads deep jade.

Gate stills f16/f75/f140 and strip f62-64 were rendered one or two script revisions before the final. The intervening changes (heart rock end and heart motion-blur keying) do not affect those frames' content. Strip f61, f65-72 and the full preview are from the final script.
dopa_bugs: Storyboard spec (not lib/dopa.py): clamp_indirect=20 for S02 suppresses all refractive caustics from a 5 cm orb, whose radiance is about 250. Worked around with S02_CLAMP=0. The lead may want to check other shots that rely on caustics, such as S03's lime caustic under the gummy with clamp_indirect=10.

D.mat_glass / D.mat_jelly set Principled 'Base Color' to the tint. Cycles applies it at both interfaces of a closed solid, so the perceived glass and caustic colour is the palette colour squared (lemon reads amber, pink reads dark red). Worked around in-script by setting the base colour to colour^0.5 (candy_glass helper). S03's lime gummy (D.mat_glass) has the same effect.

Storyboard S02/S03 circle-match distances (0.556 m, 0.59 m) use the small-angle silhouette r/d. The exact sphere silhouette at close range is larger (40 mm at 0.556 m gives about 1645 px). S03 should compute d = r / sin(atan(0.8 * 18 / lens)), or measure with a mask pass as done here.
No dopa bug proper. Missing features that were worked around in-script: a glossy-only world strength in D.world_hdri, and per-object ray-visibility and emission_sampling helpers.
self_critique:
The shot now proves C2 at the poster-still level in the macro and at final quality. One small orb lights everything, and each glass candy throws its own tinted caustic: a hot lemon focal spot, a pink heart caustic and an aqua crescent. They land on the beat (31/46/61) and crawl left as the orb arcs. The 2048-spp frames are clean, with no fireflies and no blotch boiling in the caustics.

The biggest lesson was the storyboard's clamp_indirect=20. It silently scaled every caustic down about 14x, and I spent several rounds tuning geometry before finding it. Measuring a single caustic sample's value earlier would have saved roughly 30 minutes.

The wide frames read as a premium toy diorama: a mint jewel-box, a chrome lollipop swirl, a candy-sky mirror ball on a coral pedestal, and a puffy pink heart. But the caustics are small there (about 40-80 px). The bunny's rainbow sparkle on the plinth is too faint for its f16 beat, and the pool near the orb runs hotter than spec.

The end push hits the circle match exactly (1535.7 px geometric, centred). The last frames are an intentional but heavy zoom blur, so S03 must mirror it.

Cost is the main risk: about 43 s/f in the macro is marginally over target. The fixes that got there are documented in the header: no clamp, card not sampled as a light, decays ending at zero crossings, keyed heart motion blur.

If I had another hour, I would:
- Lift the bunny sparkle with a small rim-light-free spot aim or a larger bunny.
- Lower the pool near the orb by 10-15%.
- Try 1536 spp on the macro to get under 40 s/f.
